elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement for convenience during the committed term.
elements.evidence: Section 11.1 expressly permits Customer to terminate the Agreement during the Term for convenience.

elements.element: Customer may exercise its convenience-termination right on 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: Section 11.1 requires at least 30 days' written notice to M&I.

elements.element: Customer is not required to pay an early-termination fee or equivalent termination-specific charge for exercising the convenience-termination right.
elements.evidence: Although the first sentence says Customer pays “no early termination fee,” the retained language says the Termination for Convenience Fee “shall apply,” requires two 50% payments, and separately requires payment of unamortized costs and disposition expenses. The free-exit obligation is therefore contradictory and incomplete.

elements.element: Vendor must provide Customer a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees following Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Section 11.1 expressly requires M&I to pay Customer a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, although no payment deadline is stated.

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right, including a right to withdraw Services for convenience, during the committed term.
elements.evidence: Section 10.2 negates only M&I's withdrawal of non-Core Services upon 90 days' notice. It is not a categorical prohibition on all Vendor convenience termination, expressly excludes Core Services from its scope, and does not address termination of the Agreement as a whole.

elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement for convenience during the committed term.
elements.evidence: Section 11.1 expressly grants Customer a convenience-termination right during the Term.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires between 60 and 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause requires at least 30 days' written notice, which is outside the fallback range.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee payable by Customer does not exceed three months' fees.
elements.evidence: No operative three-month cap appears. The clause inconsistently states that no fee is payable while retaining language that the fee applies and is paid in two installments, and it imposes additional uncapped unamortized costs and disposition expenses.

elements.element: Vendor has a termination-for-convenience right exercisable at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: The rendered language does not grant M&I a convenience-termination right at the end of a term; it addresses only during-Term withdrawal of certain Services.

elements.element: Vendor may not exercise any termination-for-convenience right before the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Section 10.2 only restricts withdrawal of non-Core Services upon 90 days' notice and does not comprehensively prohibit all Vendor convenience termination before term-end.

elements.element: Vendor must give 90 days' notice of any permitted end-of-term convenience termination.
elements.evidence: The 90-day period appears only in the negated during-Term service-withdrawal provision; it is not attached to a permitted end-of-term termination right.

result.reason: The redline correctly adds Customer's 30-day written-notice right and a pro-rata refund, but it leaves contradictory fee applicability, payment mechanics, and uncapped termination-related costs. The Vendor restriction is limited and awkwardly drafted rather than categorical. It also supplies neither the fallback notice period and fee cap nor a properly bounded end-of-term Vendor termination right. Obsolete fee mechanics and the Estimated Remaining Value definition remain, so the drafting is neither complete nor internally consistent.
